messages:
emily_csm: quick heads-up on Arborly — during yesterday's onboarding run we saw 95th/99th p50 spikes on the chat endpoint, their UI is pretty sensitive to tails :grimace:

emily_csm: baseline was ~120ms p95 but yesterday jumped to ~420ms p99 for a subset of sessions (esp long-history users). They mentioned renewal in Q3, want to avoid any negative first impressions.

sanjay_se: thanks for flagging. do we have request ids or sample traces? that helps decide quant vs routing.

emily_csm: pasted two request IDs from their logs: `req_0xA1B2` and `req_0xA1B3`. attaching the small trace we got:```
2026-03-20T18:02:11Z req_0xA1B2 model:redwood-3-large seq_len:1024 tokens:480 latency_ms:412 tail_op:kv_cache_miss
2026-03-20T18:02:13Z req_0xA1B3 model:redwood-3-large seq_len:128 tokens:64 latency_ms:195 tail_op:quant_slow_path
```

emily_csm: they are on Hosted with default routing (latency-preferred) and no prefix caching enabled.

rachel_eng: interesting — kv_cache_miss on long-history sessions is suspect. prefix caching could shave a lot off those long requests. also `quant_slow_path` suggests their model variant on the serving fleet is hitting a non-optimized kernel for int8 path.

rachel_eng: quick proposal: 1) enable prefix/KV caching for the chat route (safe) 2) canary a 5% traffic shift to `rw-infer-int8-v2` (our vetted int8 build) 3) add a routing rule to prefer dedicated-capacity if p99 > 300ms for >5mins.

sanjay_se: +1. can we do the canary as a shadow first? mirror 100% but only send 5% to the int8 variant for responses so we can validate quality. we should run automated evals on our sample prompts.

kai_enablement: I'll coordinate a short enablement session with the Arborly eng lead tomorrow to explain tradeoffs. suggest we share quick A/B quality metrics and token-cost delta.

emily_csm: good. also want to prep renewal doc: mention expected cost drop (~18-25%) if int8 passes QA, and p99 improvement numbers from similar customers.

rachel_eng: note on implementation — for the canary we'll apply this config:```
route: /api/chat.arborly
traffic_split:
  - variant: redwood-3-large (control) weight:95
  - variant: rw-infer-int8-v2 (canary) weight:5
mirror: true
kv_cache: enabled prefix_size: 256MB
canary_metrics: [p50,p95,p99,rogue_token_rate,token_cost]
```

rachel_eng: I'll spin up the canary config in the staging branch, tag `canary/arborly/2026-03-21`. deploy-bot will notify on rollout.

deploy-bot: rollout created -> canary/arborly/2026-03-21 (staging). checks: infra-health ✅, model-compat ✅, evals queued.

sanjay_se: for quality evals, use the Arborly anonymized prompt set + synthetic edge-cases (long-history replies). target: <1% semantic delta and <400ms p99 on int8.

emily_csm: timeline? Arborly is doing live traffic ramp next week, would love canary in prod by Thursday if safe.

rachel_eng: timeline looks tight but doable: staging canary today, evaluate tomorrow morning, small prod canary Thursday 10am UTC if evals green. I'll add a rollback-on-regression policy (auto-fallback to control).

kai_enablement: I'll run the 30-min walkthrough with the customer on Wed and share the expected dashboards (p95/p99 token-cost).

emily_csm: action items: Rachel -> deploy staging canary + enable prefix caching (done), Sanjay -> run eval suite and post results, Kai -> customer walkthrough Wed 11am UTC, Emily -> update renewal note with numbers.

sanjay_se: starting evals now, will post artifacts and diff report to this thread. :rocket:

emily_csm: thanks team — keeping Arborly in a green experience bucket is top priority. ping me if anything blocks the prod canary. :eyes:
